resources.string: Your next good habit starts with one item.
%1$d XP to your next level. Keep growing!
Empty your bottles before recycling. Check local rules and deposit-return labels.
Learn a little. Change a lot.
Bite-sized lessons for a healthier planet.
What should you do with a plastic bottle?
Your progress is saved. New correct answers earn 20 XP.
Every item has a next chapter.
Choose a clear photo of one item. Recognition runs on your device.
Could not read this photo. Please try another image.
No reliable match. Try a close-up on a plain background, or choose the material.
A photo cannot always distinguish materials. Check the item before choosing a bin.
Empty the packaging. Check for a deposit-return symbol first. Put accepted packaging in your local plastics collection; keep other plastics separate.
Empty the container. Return deposit bottles where applicable. Use the glass packaging collection. Ceramics, mirrors and drinking glasses need separate disposal.
Keep paper clean and dry. Flatten boxes and remove plastic inserts. Put clean paper and cardboard in the paper collection.
Empty the packaging and check deposit-return markings. Use the locally designated metal packaging collection. Do not include pressurised or hazardous containers.
Never put batteries in household recycling or general waste. Tape exposed terminals and take them to a dedicated battery collection point.
Use an approved e-waste collection point or retailer take-back. Remove personal data. Remove batteries only if designed to be safely removable.
Separate packaging. Use your local food-waste or compost collection if available. Follow local rules for meat and cooked food.
Do not guess the bin from an uncertain photo. Check the material marking or ask your local waste provider.
Bin colours and accepted materials vary by municipality. Confirm local rules before disposal.
Approximate IP area: %1$s. This may be inaccurate with a VPN.
Allow approximate location to find nearby drop-offs. Without it, your public IP estimates your area using ipwho.is.
Location permission is disabled. You can enable it in Android settings, or keep using the approximate IP area.
No mapped collection points within 10 km. Move the map and search another area.
Could not load locations. Check your connection and retry.
Could not estimate your location. Move the map to your area and tap Search this map area.
Not listed — check with the operator
© OpenStreetMap contributors · Verify access and opening hours before visiting.
Maps use OpenStreetMap and Overpass. Without location permission, ipwho.is receives your public IP to estimate your area.
Example scores. Your XP is saved on this device.
Cloud sign-in needs the Firebase project configuration. Your learning progress works without an account.
Enter a valid email and a password with at least 8 characters.
Could not sign in. Check your details, connection and account configuration.
Account created. You are signed in.
Learning progress is stored on this device.
An internet connection is required to load the map.
Drag a rectangle around one item, including its recycling code. The green frame is the area used for recognition.
Photo crop. For precise selection, take a closer photo of one item.
Several items were found. Refine the crop to choose one before selecting a disposal guide.
For best results, photograph one item close up, with its material code visible. Crop out other objects and hands.

Take the complete device to a vape take-back or electrical-waste collection point that accepts vapes. Never put it in general waste or household recycling. Do not puncture or dismantle it to remove a built-in battery. If you photographed only its box, choose the packaging material instead.
The model could not make a reliable match. Try a clear close-up or select the item below.
Identified using visible text or markings. Check that the photo shows the device, rather than just its packaging.
Visual recognition is temporarily unavailable. Try again when Google Play services has finished setting up the recognition runtime. Any guidance below is based on visible markings.
Batteries need dedicated collection because damaged cells can cause fires.
Empty packaging helps keep the recycling stream clean. Check local rules for lids and deposit returns.
Clean, dry cardboard can become new paper products. Wet or food-soiled cardboard may need another collection stream.
Matched one of your saved examples. Please confirm the item.
Example learned on this device. Similar photos can now be suggested.
Item selected. Could not save a visual example; try scanning again.
%1$d saved examples · Stored only on this device. Similarity matching improves with clear examples from different angles.
Remove all saved photo examples from this device?
Estimate for recycling instead of landfill, using EPA WARM v16 US averages and the weight you enter. Local outcomes differ. A photo cannot measure weight or prove recycling.
No reliable CO₂ estimate for this item. Correct collection still matters, especially for devices and batteries.
Confirm this exact material before estimating; other plastics, metals and paper types use different factors.
I recycled this item · Save estimate
Recycling entry saved. This is an estimated benefit, not a verified carbon credit.
Enter a weight between 0 and 1,000,000 grams.
%1$s kg CO₂e · estimated from your recycling entries
Area not found or service unavailable. Try a city and country, or move the map manually.
Enter a city or postcode first.
Map tiles: OpenStreetMap. Collection points: Overpass. City search: Nominatim. Without location permission, ipwho.is estimates your area from your public IP.
Map services cannot be reached. Check your connection, keep the app open and retry.
Looks similar to labeled reference photos. Check the material before sorting.
